common_issues: THREE duplicates with batch 1 in this single batch: 'semolina', 'flattened rice', and 'refined wheat flour' all appear identically. Total known cross-batch duplicates now: green peas (1↔2), green chilli (2↔6), sugar (6↔8), semolina (1↔9), flattened rice (1↔9), refined wheat flour (1↔9). Run a name-uniqueness check across the full dataset before final import — this is a systemic data-prep issue, not isolated errors.

Allergen tagging mostly excellent — special credit for: rolled oats tagged gluten (correct for default Indian commercial oats which aren't certified GF), besan correctly empty (chickpea flour, no gluten — common false-positive), sabudana correctly empty (tapioca, no gluten). One critical miss: corn flakes should be tagged gluten because commercial brands (Kellogg's, including Indian market) contain barley-derived malt flavoring.

Bread entry has unit semantics issue: 'piece' = 50g = '2 bread slices' conflicts with 'piece' convention used elsewhere (1 of something). Recipe authors will likely misinterpret '2 piece bread' as 100g when they mean 50g.

issues.problem: 1 cup besan = 120g is on the high side. USDA chickpea flour = 92g/cup; Indian cooking references span 100-130g/cup depending on milling fineness. 120g is defensible for loosely-packed coarse besan but high for finely-milled.
issues.suggested_fix: Borderline — leave at 120g (Indian-reference) or change to 100g (mid-range). Both defensible.

issues.problem: DUPLICATE — 'semolina' appeared identically in batch 1 (same katori=95g, cup=160g, tbsp=10g, gluten allergen). Same situation as the green peas / green chilli / sugar duplicates.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop from one of the two batches before merging. Either keep this in 'processed staples' or in 'grains/flours' but not both.

issues.problem: DUPLICATE — 'flattened rice' appeared identically in batch 1 (same katori=20g, cup=50g, tbsp=3g). Note: in batch 1 I flagged these as low (medium poha is ~33g/katori, ~55g/cup) and they were corrected in the batch 1 output. This batch's entry still has the original low values.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop from one of the two batches. If keeping this entry, also apply the batch 1 corrections (katori=33, cup=55).

issues.problem: DUPLICATE — 'refined wheat flour' appeared identically in batch 1 (same katori=80g, cup=125g, tbsp=8g, gluten allergen).
issues.suggested_fix: Drop from one of the two batches.

issues.problem: All three sabudana unit weights are ~10-15% on the low side at density ~0.65 g/ml (katori should be ~98g, cup ~155g, tbsp ~10g). Defensible since sabudana packing varies with pearl size.
issues.suggested_fix: Borderline — leave as-is or bump slightly. Current values are within plausible range.

issues.problem: 'raw papad' is good ('raw' here meaning unroasted/unfried, which matters nutritionally since fried papad is ~2x calories). Already close to normalised form.
issues.suggested_fix: canonical_form='raw' (drop the leading 'raw' redundancy and let typical_form_note carry 'uncooked' detail).

issues.problem: 'piece' = 50g with notes '2 bread slices' is semantically problematic. Throughout the rest of the dataset 'piece' means '1 of something' (1 onion, 1 mango, 1 papad, etc.). Defining 'piece' = '2 slices' will cause recipe authors to enter '2 piece bread' meaning 2 slices but the system will compute 100g = 4 slices. Either remove this unit or rename to a non-conflicting label.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the 'piece' unit entirely. 'slice' already handles single-slice cases; if a 2-slice convenience unit is needed, name it 'pair' or 'double slice'. The cup unit (cubed) covers other use cases.

issues.problem: Missing 'gluten' allergen tag. Corn flakes are made from corn (naturally gluten-free), BUT commercial brands universally use barley-derived malt flavoring for color/flavor — including Kellogg's (the dominant Indian brand). Per celiac.org and Coeliac UK, mainstream corn flakes are NOT gluten-free. A user with celiac disease seeing common_allergens=[] for corn flakes could have a serious reaction. This is a safety issue, not just a labeling preference.
issues.suggested_fix: Change to common_allergens=['gluten']. If you want to separately model gluten-free corn flakes (e.g., Nature's Path GF cornflakes, available in India), create a separate ingredient entry.
